title: Missing worker/process/event-loop metrics are coerced to 0, so the benchmark can report a pass without having measured them
test: tests/benchmarkRuntime.test.js: 'benchmark fails closed and reports null when worker, process, RSS and event-loop metrics are absent' (plus 'only one sample lacks the event-loop delay' and 'worker usage lacks the system CPU time'); tests/churnRuntime.test.js: 'churn harness fails with explicit unavailable failures when heap, resource, room and socket metrics are absent' (plus the baseline-only and settled-only cases); unit tests in tests/runtimeBenchmarkModel.test.js for the new helpers
proof: Harness-level tests run scripts/benchmark-runtime.js and scripts/churn-runtime.js against a fixture server (socket.io acknowledgements plus /api/metrics) whose metrics lack the fields. On the unchanged code the benchmark case failed with 'Expected values to be strictly equal: 0 !== 1' (the run exited 0 with pass true, observed values 0 and headroom 100); the one-sample event-loop case and the missing-ru_stime case failed the same way; the churn all-absent case failed with '0 !== 1' (exit 0, pass true, zero growth), the settled-only case likewise, and the baseline-only case reported only a spurious 'active sockets grew by 4 (limit 0)' with the missing heap passing silently. After the fix: worker CPU, process CPU, RSS growth and event-loop p95/max are null when any input is missing, headroom for them is null, and the run exits 1 with '<metric> unavailable' failures (media-worker CPU, Node process CPU, RSS growth, event-loop p95, event-loop max); churn computes heap growth, resource growth, active rooms and socket growth as null when the baseline or settled field is absent and fails with 'heap growth unavailable', 'active resource growth unavailable', 'rooms active after settle unavailable' and 'active socket growth unavailable'. A complete-metrics fixture still passes in both harnesses with measured values. Also checked against the real server (spawned in test mode): /api/metrics reports every field, and a benchmark run against it produced only topology failures, no 'unavailable'.
